GaussianChannelGen.role: Gaussian channel for an arbitrary measurable input signal
GaussianChannelGen.assessment: Reviewed all statements and chanW/quadW/outVarW. The input space is general measurable alpha; a measurable real signal w determines the Gaussian kernel. Nonzero noise and MemLp(w,2,P) yield the exact comparison KL. This supports the vector construction without requiring independent input coordinates.
obligations: Actual signal and conditional noise are physical bindings; these are actual Gaussian-kernel theorems rather than an assumed channel-cap inequality.

GaussianVector.role: Finite vector Gaussian kernel with correlated signal
GaussianVector.assessment: Reviewed all statements and the recursive product channel/reference measures. The noise coordinates are conditionally product given arbitrary shared input; signal coordinates may be correlated. Measurable-equivalence, KL additivity and scalar KL establish the sum-log bound and the trace bound with second moments.
obligations: The physical channel must instantiate the constructed noise kernel; the later whitening theorem covers positive-definite correlated noise.

Whitening.role: Correlated Gaussian noise and information invariance
Whitening.assessment: Reviewed all statements, wht, whtEquiv, corrChan and whtSignal. Positive-definite covariance has an invertible square root; the measurable linear inverse whitens the actual multivariate Gaussian. Mutual information is invariant under that output equivalence, and the whitened coordinate bound yields the correlated channel result.
obligations: The full conditional covariance must be positive definite after all permitted side information. Marginal noise variances are insufficient.

Rotation.role: Orthogonal output rotation and Gaussian channel bound
Rotation.assessment: Reviewed all statements and rotEquiv/rotSignal. Isometry preserves identity-covariance Gaussian noise and information under the invertible output map. The rotated bound applies to actual rotated/whitened coordinate variances, retaining all signal correlation.
obligations: Apply the supplied isometry to the full joint signal and preserve moment/measurement conditions.

LogDet.role: Exact full-covariance Gaussian log-determinant upper bound
LogDet.assessment: Reviewed all statements and cov. The covariance quadratic form is derived from finite second moments; an orthonormal eigenbasis diagonalises its variances. The determinant product identity turns the rotated sum-log bound into the exact log-det bound for the actual correlated Gaussian kernel.
obligations: Connect the actual whitened covariance to the gain/noise/range estimate in AreaBridge. The manuscript's bits convention divides the native nats bound by ln 2.
